members.closest_existing_considered: `PresentedGroup rels` and finite-generation predicates in `Mathlib.GroupTheory.PresentedGroup` and `Mathlib.GroupTheory.Finiteness`; categorical and module/ring finite-presentation notions are not the abstract-group notion required here.
members.code:
def IsFinitelyPresented (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧ Nonempty (G ≃* PresentedGroup rels)
members.docstring:
A group `G` is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to a group given by finitely many
generators and finitely many relators.

members.docstring:
A group $G$ is finitely presented if it is isomorphic to
$\langle x_1, \ldots, x_k \mid R \rangle$ for some $k$ and some finite set $R$ of relators in
the free group on $x_1, \ldots, x_k$.
members.meaning: The group is isomorphic to PresentedGroup rels for some k and finite set rels of relators in FreeGroup (Fin k).
members.name: IsFinitelyPresented
members.title: Conjecture 10.36
members.why: Same data (Fin k generators, finite Set of relators) but the isomorphism is stated as PresentedGroup rels ≃* G instead of G ≃* PresentedGroup rels; equivalent via MulEquiv.symm.

members.closest_existing_considered: Group.FG (only finite generation, strictly weaker); PresentedGroup (used as the building block); Module.FinitePresentation (module analogue, not applicable to groups).
members.docstring:
A group $G$ is *finitely presented* if it is isomorphic to a group
$\langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid r_1, \dots, r_m \rangle$ given by finitely many generators
$x_1, \dots, x_n$ and finitely many relators $r_1, \dots, r_m$, i.e. to a quotient of the free
group on `Fin n` by the normal closure of a finite set of relators.
members.meaning: Isomorphic to PresentedGroup of a finite set of relators in the free group on Fin n.
members.name: IsFinitelyPresented
members.title: Conjecture 10.71
members.why: Uses a Finset of relators (coerced to a Set) instead of a finite Set, and the isomorphism is reversed (PresentedGroup ↑rels ≃* G); both differences are equivalence-preserving.

members.why: Quantifies over an arbitrary finite type α : Type (with Finite α as an existential witness) instead of Fin n, and states the iso as PresentedGroup rels ≃* G. Equivalent via Finite.equivFin + PresentedGroup.equivPresentedGroup (relator set stays finite) and MulEquiv.symm.

groups.notes: Representative switched from kourovka-10.11 (arbitrary finite type α : Type) to kourovka-4.11 (Fin n generators, finite Set of relators, G ≃* PresentedGroup rels), which is the majority form. All 12 variants are mutually equivalent: differences are only iso direction, Finset vs Set.Finite, and Fin n vs an arbitrary finite type in Type 0 (transported via PresentedGroup.equivPresentedGroup with Finite.equivFin). None of them is in Mathlib; Mathlib only has PresentedGroup and Group.FG.

def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N
members.docstring:
A group $G$ is *residually finite* if for every $g \in G$ with $g \neq 1$ there is a
normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq G$ of finite index with $g \notin N$.
members.meaning: Every non-identity element lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index.
members.name: IsResiduallyFinite
members.title: Conjecture 1.31

of elements of `G` for the variables, i.e. `f w = 1` for every homomorphism

def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (e : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk e.1) = FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk e.2)
members.docstring:
A group `G` satisfies the identity $u = v$ if $u$ and $v$ take the same value in `G` for
every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$.
members.meaning: The two words take the same value under every assignment of the variables in G.
members.name: SatisfiesIdentity
members.title: Conjecture 7.23
members.why: Takes an identity `u = v` given as a pair of raw letter lists `List (ℕ × Bool) × List (ℕ × Bool)` (via `FreeGroup.mk`) and asks `lift f (mk u) = lift f (mk v)`, rather than a single word `w : FreeGroup ℕ` with `lift f w = 1`; the input types differ so neither can be substituted for the other, even though every law w = 1 corresponds to the identity (w, []) and vice versa via u v⁻¹.

groups.notes: Two flavours occur: quantifying over substitutions `f : ℕ → G` (evaluated via `FreeGroup.lift f`) and quantifying over homomorphisms `φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`. They are propositionally equivalent because `FreeGroup.lift : (ℕ → G) ≃ (FreeGroup ℕ →* G)` is a bijection, but not definitionally equal. 6.47 generalizes the alphabet to an arbitrary type ι (definitionally the representative at ι = ℕ). 7.23 uses a genuinely different input type (an identity u = v given as a pair of raw letter lists) rather than a single word w = 1.

members.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.UnitDistanceEmbeddable` / `UnitDistancePlaneGraph` in FormalConjecturesForMathlib (only place vertices in ℝ², no edge arcs or crossing conditions); Mathlib `Path`/`unitInterval` used as building blocks.
members.code:
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → ℝ²) (γ : G.edgeSet → I → ℝ²),
    Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ e, Continuous (γ e) ∧ Function.Injective (γ e)) ∧
    (∀ e : G.edgeSet, s(γ e 0, γ e 1) = (e : Sym2 V).map f) ∧
    (∀ e, ∀ t, t ≠ 0 → t ≠ 1 → γ e t ∉ Set.range f) ∧
    (∀ e e', e ≠ e' → ∀ t t', t ≠ 0 → t ≠ 1 → γ e t ≠ γ e' t')
members.docstring:
A graph `G` is *planar* if it has a drawing in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$: the vertices are
sent to distinct points and each edge is sent to an arc (an injective continuous image of the unit
interval) joining the images of its two ends. The interior of an arc contains no vertex, and the
interior of an arc meets no other arc. Two distinct arcs thus meet only in common endpoints.

By Wagner's theorem a finite graph is planar in this sense exactly when it has neither $K_5$
nor $K_{3,3}$ as a minor.
members.meaning: There exist an injective vertex map to ℝ² and injective continuous arcs for edges joining their endpoints, with arc interiors avoiding vertices and other arcs.
members.name: IsPlanar
members.title: Apex graphs and Jørgensen's conjecture

members.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib (`rg -i planar|Kuratowski|Wagner|minor` in Mathlib/Combinatorics) and the repo: only unrelated matroid minors and a TODO mention in Coloring.lean; nothing usable.

  Nonempty (PlanarEmbedding G)
members.docstring: A simple graph is planar if it has a planar embedding in the Euclidean plane.
members.meaning: The graph admits a crossing-free drawing in the plane.
members.name: IsPlanar
members.title: Barnette's conjecture
members.why: Same data (injective vertex map, continuous injective arc per edge of G.edgeSet). arc_zero_one (∃ u v, e = s(u,v) ∧ ends) is equivalent to s(arc 0, arc 1) = e.map vertex; 'vertex w ∈ range arc → w ∈ e' is equivalent to 'interior points avoid range vertex' given injectivity of the arc and the endpoint condition; 'range ∩ range ⊆ range vertex' is equivalent to 'interior of one arc misses the other arc'. Not defeq (structure vs ∃, different formulations).

members.why: Same data with arcs packaged as C(I, ℝ²) instead of a function plus continuity proof; arc_ends is literally the representative's endpoint condition; arc_vertex (arc e t ∈ range vertex → t = 0 ∨ t = 1) is the contrapositive of the representative's interior condition; arc_inter (range ∩ range ⊆ range vertex) is equivalent to the representative's pointwise crossing condition given the other axioms. Not defeq (Nonempty structure, C(I,ℝ²), reformulated conditions).

members.name: IsPlanar

members.why: EmbedsIn G ℝ² is the same ∃-statement with arcs as C(unitInterval, ℝ²), the endpoint equation written in the other direction, the vertex condition in range/membership form (f v ∈ range (γ e) → v ∈ e) and the crossing condition in range form (range ∩ range ⊆ range f); these are equivalent to the representative's pointwise interior conditions but not syntactically/defeq the same.

def IsPlanar : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : V → ℝ²) (arc : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²), IsPlanarDrawing G f arc
members.docstring: A graph is planar if it has a planar drawing in the plane.
members.meaning: There exist a vertex placement and arc assignment forming a crossing-free drawing of G.
members.name: IsPlanar
members.title: Harborth's conjecture
members.why: Arcs are given as sets `arc : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²` (arbitrary on non-edges) each required to be the range of an injective Path from f u to f v for every adjacent pair, with vertex-avoidance (f w ∉ arc s(u,v) for w ≠ u,v) and intersection contained in f '' ({u,v} ∩ {u',v'}). Choosing an orientation of each edge (and possibly reversing the path) converts to the representative's edge-indexed parametrised arcs and back; the conditions are equivalent given injectivity and the endpoint equation. Clearly not defeq.

members.closest_existing_considered: Kuratowski/Wagner characterisations would require graph minors or subdivisions, also absent from Mathlib.
members.code:
def Planar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  EmbedsIn G (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))
members.docstring: A simple graph is *planar* if it embeds in the plane $\mathbb{R}^2$.
members.meaning: The graph embeds in ℝ².
members.name: Planar
members.title: Negami's conjecture
members.why: Planar G = Nonempty (Drawing G (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))): arcs are oriented Paths indexed by G.Adj u v with a compatibility field edge_symm; edge_ne_vertex and edge_disjoint are exactly the representative's pointwise interior conditions transported to the adjacency indexing. From a representative embedding one builds the oriented paths (reversing when the arc runs from f v to f u), which automatically satisfy edge_symm; conversely pick an orientation per edge. Same notion, not defeq.

members.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Coloring` docstring mentions planar graphs only as a TODO; nothing exists in FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
members.code:
def IsPlanar (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f A, IsPlaneDrawing G f A
members.docstring: A simple graph is *planar* if it has a crossing-free drawing in the plane.
members.meaning: There exist a placement and arcs forming a crossing-free drawing of G.
members.name: IsPlanar
members.title: Universal point set
members.why: Same shape as Harborth: curves as sets `A : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²`, each the range of an injective Path between the endpoint images for adjacent u v, with `f w ∈ A e → w ∈ e` for edges e and `A e₁ ∩ A e₂ ⊆ f '' {w | w ∈ e₁ ∧ w ∈ e₂}` for distinct edges. Orienting each edge converts to/from the representative's edge-indexed parametrised arcs; conditions equivalent given injectivity and endpoints. Not defeq.

groups.notes: All seven are the same notion: existence of a topological embedding of G in the plane (injective vertex map, one simple arc per edge joining the images of its endpoints, arcs meeting vertices only at their own endpoints, distinct arcs meeting only in common endpoint images). The differences are only in packaging: pointwise interior conditions (representative, Negami) vs range-based conditions (Barnette, EarthMoon, Grunbaum), arcs indexed by G.edgeSet vs by G.Adj u v (Negami, with a redundant edge_symm compatibility field that is always satisfiable) vs arc *sets* indexed by Sym2 V (Harborth, UniversalPointSet), `∃ ... ∧ ...` vs `Nonempty structure`. None is defeq to the representative; all are provably equivalent. The check files assume every file's local notation `ℝ²` means `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` (Negami writes this explicitly); if some file used `ℝ × ℝ` instead the notions would still be equivalent (homeomorphic planes) but the supplied proofs would need a transport step.

groups.concept: quasi-identity in the language of groups
labels: quasi-identity in the language of groups

members.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula (Mathlib.ModelTheory) — no group language, no Horn-formula notion; would be far heavier and less transparent.
members.code:
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The number $m$ of premises. -/
  numPremises : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_i = v_i$, each given as the pair of words $(u_i, v_i)$. -/
  premise : Fin numPremises → FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, given as the pair of words $(u, v)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)
members.docstring:
A quasi-identity in the language of groups: a universal Horn sentence
$\forall x_1 \dots x_n\ (u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_m = v_m \to u = v)$, where
$u_1, v_1, \dots, u_m, v_m, u, v$ are elements of the free group on the $n$ variables
$x_1, \dots, x_n$.
members.meaning: Syntactic universal Horn sentence with finitely many variables, finitely many premise equations and one conclusion equation between free-group words.
members.name: QuasiIdentity
members.title: Conjecture 10.10

members.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language / FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula (Mathlib.ModelTheory): only ring and field languages exist (Language.ring), no group language and no Horn-formula predicate; FreeGroup (used as the term algebra).
members.code:
structure GroupQuasiIdentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_1 = v_1, \dots, u_m = v_m$, as pairs of group words. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as a pair of group words. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)
members.docstring:
A quasi-identity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$\forall \bar x \;
  \bigl(u_1(\bar x) = v_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge u_m(\bar x) = v_m(\bar x)
  \;\to\; u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)\bigr).$$
The group words $u_i, v_i, u, v$ are recorded as elements of the free group on `Fin n`;
two group words define the same element of the free group exactly when they take the same
value in every group, so this loses nothing. The list of premises may be empty, in which
case the quasi-identity is an identity.
members.meaning: A number of variables, a finite list of premise equations and a conclusion equation between free-group words.
members.name: GroupQuasiIdentity
members.title: Conjecture 7.45
members.why: Same data (n variables, conclusion pair in FreeGroup (Fin n)²) but premises stored as a List instead of a Fin m-indexed family; these are canonically in bijection via List.equivSigmaTuple, so the two types are equivalent (not defeq).

members.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib.ModelTheory (FirstOrder.Language.Sentence, BoundedFormula) — but Mathlib only provides `Language.ring`, no group language, and building one plus universal-Horn syntax would be far heavier than the free-group representation, which is the standard way quasiidentities of groups are written.
members.code:
structure Quasiidentity where
  /-- The number $n$ of variables. -/
  numVars : ℕ
  /-- The premises $u_i = v_i$, as pairs of words $(u_i, v_i)$. -/
  premises : List (FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars))
  /-- The conclusion $u = v$, as the pair of words $(u, v)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup (Fin numVars) × FreeGroup (Fin numVars)
members.docstring:
A quasiidentity in the language of groups, in the variables $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$:
$$(u_1 = v_1 \wedge \dots \wedge u_k = v_k) \to u = v,$$
where $u_1, v_1, \dots, u_k, v_k, u, v$ are group words in $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$. Whether a group
satisfies such a formula depends only on the classes of these words modulo the group axioms, so
the words are represented as elements of the free group on `Fin n`. The case $k = 0$ (no premises)
gives the identities.
members.meaning: A universal Horn sentence with n variables, a list of premise equations u_i = v_i and a conclusion u = v, words in the free group on Fin n.
members.name: Quasiidentity
members.title: Conjecture 8.64
members.why: Textually identical to the 7.45 variant (numVars, List of premise pairs, conclusion pair); differs from the representative only in storing the premises as a List instead of a Fin m-indexed family, which is a canonical bijection (List.equivSigmaTuple).

members.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Sentence`/`Structure.Realize` (no group language in Mathlib), `FreeGroup.lift` (used for evaluation).
members.code:
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The words `wᵢ` of the premises `wᵢ = 1`. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word `w` of the conclusion `w = 1`. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ
members.docstring:
A quasi-identity in the language of groups, in the variables `x₀, x₁, x₂, …`:
finitely many premises `wᵢ = 1` and one conclusion `w = 1`, where the `wᵢ` and `w` are
group words, i.e. elements of the free group on `ℕ`. (In a group every equation `u = v`
between words is equivalent to `u * v⁻¹ = 1`, so no generality is lost.) Identities are the
quasi-identities without premises.
members.meaning: Finitely many premises w_i = 1 and a conclusion w = 1, with words in the free group on ℕ.
members.name: QuasiIdentity
members.title: Conjecture 8.55
members.why: Different type: variables range over ℕ (no numVars), premises are a Finset (unordered, no multiplicity) of single words w (premise w = 1) rather than an indexed family of pairs (u, v), and the conclusion is a single word. Semantically it encodes the same class of sentences up to equivalence (u = v ↔ u v⁻¹ = 1), but the objects are not in bijection and cannot replace each other.

members.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Sentence / universal Horn sentences in Mathlib.ModelTheory (no group language available; no Horn-fragment notion).
members.code:
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The words `u` appearing in the premises `u = 1`. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word `w` of the conclusion `w = 1`. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ
members.docstring:
A quasi-identity in the language of groups: finitely many premises `u = 1`
(for `u ∈ premises`) and a conclusion `conclusion = 1`, all words in the variables
`x₀, x₁, …`. A quasi-identity with no premises is a law.
members.meaning: Finitely many premises u = 1 and a conclusion w = 1, words in the free group on ℕ.
members.name: QuasiIdentity
members.title: Conjecture 9.5
members.why: Textually identical to the 8.55 variant, hence differs from the representative in the same ways: words in FreeGroup ℕ (no variable count), premises a Finset of single words w (premise w = 1) instead of an indexed family of pairs, single-word conclusion. Same expressive power up to logical equivalence but a non-isomorphic type.

members.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language` / `FirstOrder.Language.Sentence` (Mathlib only provides ring/field languages, no group language, and no notion of Horn/quasi-identity shape); `FreeGroup` (used as the term representation).
members.code:
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The premises $t_1 = s_1, \dots, t_k = s_k$, as pairs of words $(t_i, s_i)$. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion $t = s$, as the pair of words $(t, s)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ
members.docstring:
A quasi-identity in the signature of groups,
$$\forall \bar x\ \bigl(t_1 = s_1 \wedge \dots \wedge t_k = s_k \to t = s\bigr), \qquad k \ge 0.$$
The premises $t_i = s_i$ and the conclusion $t = s$ are equations between group words in the
variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group word is represented by the element of the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ` it defines, since two words take the same value in every group under every
assignment of the variables exactly when they define the same element of the free group.
The case $k = 0$ is an identity.
members.meaning: A finite set of premise equations and a conclusion equation between words in the free group on ℕ.
members.name: QuasiIdentity
members.title: Conjecture 9.6
members.why: Keeps premises/conclusion as pairs (t, s) like the representative, but words live in FreeGroup ℕ (no numVars) and premises form a Finset (unordered, duplicate-free) rather than a Fin m-indexed family; no bijection with the representative type, though it encodes the same class of sentences.

groups.notes: All six are Type-valued syntactic encodings of "quasi-identity of groups" (universal Horn sentence), and all six have the same expressive power up to logical equivalence of the encoded sentence (u = v ↔ u·v⁻¹ = 1; a word in FreeGroup ℕ mentions only finitely many variables; order/multiplicity of premises is semantically irrelevant). But as Lean objects they are not interchangeable: only 10.10, 7.45 and 8.64 are in canonical bijection (Fin m → P vs List P, via List.equivSigmaTuple). The three FreeGroup ℕ / Finset variants (8.55, 9.5, 9.6) are non-isomorphic types (unordered, duplicate-free premise sets; unbounded variable set; 8.55/9.5 additionally use one-sided premises w = 1). 7.45 and 8.64 are textually identical to each other; 8.55 and 9.5 are textually identical to each other. Any downstream `Holds`/satisfaction predicate would have to be rewritten to swap encodings.

groups.concept: satisfaction of a quasi-identity in a group
labels: satisfaction of a group quasi-identity by a group
satisfaction of a quasi-identity in a group

members.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Sentence.Realize / Theory.Model (not applicable without a group language); FreeGroup.lift.
members.code:
def GroupQuasiIdentity.Holds (q : GroupQuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2
members.docstring:
A quasi-identity $\forall \bar x\,(\bigwedge_i u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x) \to u(\bar x) = v(\bar x))$
holds in a group $G$ if for every assignment $\bar x$ of values in $G$ to the variables,
$u(\bar x) = v(\bar x)$ whenever $u_i(\bar x) = v_i(\bar x)$ for all $i$.
members.meaning: For every assignment, if all premises hold then the conclusion holds.
members.name: GroupQuasiIdentity.Holds
members.title: Conjecture 7.45

members.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.Structure.realize / `⊨` — not applicable without a group language.
members.code:
def Holds (q : Quasiidentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → G,
    (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
      FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2
members.docstring:
A group `G` satisfies the quasiidentity `q` if for every assignment `x` of the variables in `G`
under which all the premises of `q` hold, the conclusion of `q` holds. Words are evaluated at `x`
by the homomorphism `FreeGroup.lift x`.
members.meaning: For every assignment of variables under which all premises hold in G, the conclusion holds.
members.name: Holds
members.title: Conjecture 8.64
members.why: The carrier structure (numVars : ℕ, premises : List of pairs over FreeGroup (Fin numVars), conclusion pair) and the Holds body (∀ x : Fin numVars → G, all premise pairs agree under FreeGroup.lift x → conclusion pair agrees) are textually the same up to names.

members.closest_existing_considered: FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula (Mathlib.ModelTheory) — no group language, no Horn-formula notion; would be far heavier and less transparent.
members.code:
def QuasiIdentity.Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : Fin q.numVars → H,

groups.notes:
All six are the standard notion "for every assignment of the variables, if all premises evaluate true then so does the conclusion", evaluated via FreeGroup.lift, and they would agree under the evident translations of quasi-identities (List.ofFn / Finset.toList, Fin n ↪ ℕ, (u,v) ↦ u*v⁻¹). But the predicates live over five *different* carrier types for "quasi-identity", so they cannot literally replace each other. I chose 7.45 as anchor because 8.64 is textually identical to it. Independently, 8.55 and 9.5 are identical to EACH OTHER (both: premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ), conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ, ∀ x : ℕ → G, premises ↦ 1 → conclusion ↦ 1), differing only in argument order and G : Type (8.55) vs Type* (9.5). import Mathlib

structure QI where
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

def QI.Holds (q : QI) (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℕ → G, (∀ w ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x w = 1) →
    FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion = 1

def SatisfiesQI (G : Type*) [Group G] (q : QI) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, (∀ u ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift f u = 1) →
    FreeGroup.lift f q.conclusion = 1

example (q : QI) (G : Type) [Group G] : q.Holds G ↔ SatisfiesQI G q := Iff.rfl

groups.notes: The six variants fall into two families. (A) Law-defined ('equational') classes: 8.19, 8.25, 9.5 all say 'P is the class of groups killing every word of some W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ' (differences: bundled structure vs predicate, `=` of predicates vs pointwise `↔`, `FreeGroup ℕ →* G` vs `ℕ → G` — all provably equivalent; 9.5 is universe-polymorphic and coincides with the others at u = 0). (B) HSP-closed classes: 5.44 (Type u) and 7.26 (Type) are the same structure up to the universe (7.26 = 5.44.{0} after renaming G/H in mem_of_injective). (A) and (B) are equivalent mathematically by Birkhoff's HSP theorem, and the argument goes through inside a fixed `Type u` with these exact fields (relatively free groups of countable rank are small; products indexed by small types suffice), so both families define the same notion; but the proof is a substantial development (verbal subgroups, relatively free groups) that I cannot supply as a short check file, so I mark the cross-family comparisons 'unclear' rather than claim a verified equivalence. 9.68 is genuinely different: it is a *set of laws* (a presentation), not a class of groups — distinct law sets present the same variety, so equality/counting of `GroupVariety` there does not match equality/counting of varieties.

A planar embedding (a drawing without crossings) of a simple graph `G` in the Euclidean plane.

The vertices are sent to distinct points of the plane. Each edge is drawn as an arc, that is, a
continuous injective image of the unit interval `[0, 1]`, whose two ends are the images of the two
endpoints of the edge. No arc passes through the image of a vertex other than its own endpoints,
and two different arcs meet only at the images of vertices, which are then endpoints of both edges.
members.meaning: Injective vertex placement in ℝ² with continuous injective arcs for edges joining their endpoints, arcs meeting vertex points only at their own endpoints, and distinct arcs meeting only at vertex points.

A **planar drawing** of a simple graph `G`. The vertices are placed at distinct points of the
Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$. Every edge `e` is drawn as a simple arc `arc e`, a continuous
injective map from $[0,1]$ into $\mathbb{R}^2$, whose two end points are the points of the two
end vertices of `e`. An arc passes through a vertex point only at its end points, and two distinct
arcs meet only in vertex points (hence only in common end vertices).

members.title: Earth–Moon problem
members.why: Same data (injective vertex map, one continuous injective arc per element of G.edgeSet) up to bundling the continuity proof into C(I, ℝ²); the endpoint condition `s(arc e 0, arc e 1) = e.map vertex` is equivalent to the representative's `∃ u v, e = s(u,v) ∧ arc e 0 = vertex u ∧ arc e 1 = vertex v`, and `arc e t ∈ range vertex → t = 0 ∨ t = 1` is equivalent to `vertex w ∈ range (arc e) → w ∈ e` given vertex- and arc-injectivity plus the endpoint condition; the crossing conditions are literally the same.     ∃ γ : Path (pos u) (pos v), Function.Injective γ ∧ Set.range γ = arc e

A *plane drawing* of the graph `G`, that is, a realisation of `G` as a plane graph: the vertices
are distinct points `pos v` of the plane, each edge `e` is drawn as a Jordan arc `arc e` joining
the positions of its two endpoints, the interior of an arc contains no vertex, and two distinct
arcs meet only in the positions of their common endpoints.

members.why: Type-valued like the representative, but its arc data is set-valued (`G.edgeSet → Set ℝ²`, each required to be the range of some injective Path) rather than a parametrisation `I → ℝ²`, so a PlanarEmbedding determines a PlaneEmbedding (take ranges) but not conversely without choosing parametrisations — the types are not in bijection. groups.notes: All five files formalize the same informal notion (Diestel-style plane graph: injective vertex placement in ℝ², simple arcs per edge, arcs avoid non-endpoint vertices, distinct arcs meet only in common endpoints), and the induced *planarity* predicates (Nonempty of the Type-valued structures, ∃ f arc of the Prop-valued ones) are all mutually equivalent. However the definitions themselves fall into three non-interchangeable shapes: (a) Type-valued structure carrying parametrised arcs I → ℝ² (Barnette, EarthMoon — these two are in bijection); (b) Type-valued structure carrying set-valued arcs `G.edgeSet → Set ℝ²` (WordRepresentable2, additionally requiring `[DecidableEq V]`); (c) Prop-valued predicate on given data `f : V → ℝ²`, `arc : Sym2 V → Set ℝ²` (Harborth, UniversalPointSet — these two are equivalent predicates: their fields differ only by Sym2/edgeSet phrasing and `f '' ({u,v} ∩ {u',v'})` vs `f '' {w | w ∈ e₁ ∧ w ∈ e₂}`). If a common definition were introduced, the Prop-valued form (c) or a unified structure would need to be chosen; none exists in Mathlib.

def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (s : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), s 0 = ⊥ ∧ s (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, s i.castSucc ≤ s i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ)).Normal,
        IsCyclic (s i.succ ⧸ (s i.castSucc).subgroupOf (s i.succ))
members.docstring:
A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a finite subnormal series
$1 = G_0 \trianglelefteq G_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq G_n = G$, i.e. a chain of
subgroups with $G_0$ trivial, $G_n = G$ and each $G_i$ normal in $G_{i+1}$, such that every
factor group $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic.
members.meaning: There is a finite subnormal series from the trivial subgroup to the whole group all of whose successive factors are cyclic.
members.name: IsPolycyclic
members.title: Conjecture 1.31

def IsPolycyclic (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (H : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), H 0 = ⊥ ∧ H (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, H i.castSucc ≤ H i.succ ∧
      ∃ _ : ((H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ)).Normal,
        IsCyclic (H i.succ ⧸ (H i.castSucc).subgroupOf (H i.succ))
members.docstring:
A group $G$ is *polycyclic* if it has a subnormal series
$1 = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \dots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$
in which every factor $H_{i+1}/H_i$ is cyclic. Equivalently (Hirsch), $G$ is soluble and
every subgroup of $G$ is finitely generated.
members.meaning: There is a finite chain from ⊥ to ⊤ with each term normal in the next and cyclic quotients.
members.name: IsPolycyclic
members.title: Conjecture 8.2
members.why: Same formula as the representative token-for-token (only the bound name s vs H differs): ∃ n, chain H : Fin (n+1) → Subgroup G with H 0 = ⊥, H (last) = ⊤, H i ≤ H (i+1), H i normal in H (i+1) via subgroupOf, cyclic quotient.

members.closest_existing_considered: `IsSolvable` (derived series, but allows non-finitely-generated abelian factors), `Group.IsNilpotent`, `CompositionSeries` (requires maximal/simple steps, not cyclic factors).

  ∀ w ∈ W, ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = 1
members.docstring:
A group `G` *satisfies the laws* `W ⊆ FreeGroup ℕ` if every word `w ∈ W` in the variables
$x_0, x_1, \dots$ takes only the value $1$ in `G`, i.e. $w(g_0, g_1, \dots) = 1$ for every
assignment $x_i \mapsto g_i$ of the variables. The class of all groups satisfying `W` is the
variety of groups $\mathfrak{V}(W)$ defined by `W`.

members.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib for `IsRegularLocalRing`, `IsRegularRing`, `RegularLocal`, `embDim`; only `RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular` (regular sequences), `IsSMulRegular`, `IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace`, `ringKrullDim` and `Ideal.spanFinrank` exist. The alternative `(maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim R` is equivalent by Nakayama; the cotangent-space form was chosen as the canonical one.
members.code:
class IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : Prop where
  isNoetherianRing : IsNoetherianRing R
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace :
    ringKrullDim R = Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R)
members.docstring:
A local ring `R` is a *regular local ring* if it is Noetherian and its Krull dimension
$\dim R$ equals the dimension $\dim_k \mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$ of its cotangent space over
the residue field $k = R/\mathfrak{m}$ (equivalently, by Nakayama's lemma, the maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}$ can be generated by $\dim R$ elements).
members.meaning: A Noetherian local ring whose Krull dimension equals the residue-field dimension of its cotangent space m/m².
members.name: IsRegularLocalRing
members.title: Bass–Quillen conjecture

members.closest_existing_considered: IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace, ringKrullDim, IsDiscreteValuationRing (only the 1-dimensional case), IsLocalRing.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_one_iff; searched for RegularLocalRing/IsRegularLocal in Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib with no hits.
members.code:
structure IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : Prop where
  isNoetherianRing : IsNoetherianRing R
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace :
    ringKrullDim R = Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R)
members.docstring:
A local ring `R` is a *regular local ring* if it is Noetherian and its Krull dimension equals
the dimension of its cotangent space $\mathfrak{m} / \mathfrak{m}^2$ over its residue field
$R / \mathfrak{m}$.
members.meaning: A Noetherian local ring whose Krull dimension equals the residue-field dimension of its cotangent space.
members.name: IsRegularLocalRing
members.title: Resolution of singularities in characteristic $p$
members.why: Same ambient context ([CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R]) and literally the same two fields (IsNoetherianRing R and ringKrullDim R = finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R)); the only difference is the `class` vs `structure` keyword, i.e. whether an instance attribute is attached.

members.closest_existing_considered: grep for `IsRegularLocalRing`, `RegularLocal`, `embDim` in Mathlib returned nothing; `Submodule.spanFinrank` exists but an explicit Finset of generators of cardinality `ringKrullDim R` was judged more transparent.
members.code:
structure IsRegularLocalRing : Prop extends IsNoetherianRing R, IsLocalRing R where
  exists_finset_span_eq_maximalIdeal :
    ∃ s : Finset R,
      (s.card : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R ∧ Ideal.span (s : Set R) = maximalIdeal R
members.docstring:
A **regular local ring**: a Noetherian local ring $R$ whose maximal ideal can be generated by
$\dim R$ elements.
members.meaning: A Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal is generated by dim R elements.
members.name: IsRegularLocalRing
members.title: Homological conjectures in commutative algebra
variables: variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
members.why: Uses the generator formulation (∃ Finset s with |s| = dim R generating 𝔪) with IsLocalRing bundled as a parent, instead of dim R = dim_k 𝔪/𝔪². For a Noetherian local ring these agree: Nakayama gives a generating set of 𝔪 of size dim_k 𝔪/𝔪² and any generating set has ≥ that many elements, while Krull's height theorem gives dim R = ht 𝔪 ≤ μ(𝔪) = dim_k 𝔪/𝔪². Not a syntactic/defeq match; a genuine (standard) theorem is needed.

members.closest_existing_considered: IsLocalRing + IsNoetherianRing together with IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace / Module.finrank and ringKrullDim (used as building blocks); Ideal.spanFinrank of the maximal ideal (equivalent alternative by Nakayama); Mathlib's RingTheory/Regular/* (regular sequences, depth) which do not define regular local rings.
members.code:
class IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop
    extends IsLocalRing R, IsNoetherianRing R where
  finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_ringKrullDim :
    Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) = ringKrullDim R
members.docstring:
A commutative ring $R$ is a *regular local ring* if it is a Noetherian local ring whose Krull
dimension equals the dimension of its cotangent space $\mathfrak{m} / \mathfrak{m}^2$ over the
residue field $R / \mathfrak{m}$ (equivalently, by Nakayama's lemma, the maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}$ can be generated by $\dim R$ elements).
members.meaning: A Noetherian local ring whose cotangent space dimension equals its Krull dimension.
members.name: IsRegularLocalRing
members.title: Serre's positivity conjecture
members.why: Same content (Noetherian + dim R = dim_k 𝔪/𝔪²) but the `IsLocalRing R` hypothesis is bundled as a parent field instead of being a typeclass parameter, and the equation is written in the opposite direction; over any local ring the two predicates coincide (IsLocalRing is a Prop, so the bundled/ambient instances agree by proof irrelevance).

groups.notes: All four formalize the textbook notion (Noetherian local ring with dim R = dim_k 𝔪/𝔪², equivalently 𝔪 generated by dim R elements). Two present it as a class/structure over an ambient `[IsLocalRing R]` (BassQuillen, ResolutionOfSingularities — literally identical fields), two bundle `IsLocalRing R` as a parent (Serre, Homological); over a local ring all agree. The Homological variant is the only one needing real mathematics (Nakayama + Krull's height theorem). Its check file was written without access to a Lean toolchain: the Nakayama half is proved from `IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace.span_image_eq_top_iff`; the Krull half relies on the Mathlib names `IsLocalRing.ringKrullDim_eq_height_maximalIdeal`, `Ideal.height_le_spanFinrank` and `Submodule.spanFinrank_span_le_card`, whose exact spellings at the pinned checkout should be verified (the statements are in Mathlib's Krull-height-theorem / spanRank files but the names are best guesses).

groups.concept: verbal subgroup of a group determined by a set of words
labels: verbal subgroup of a group determined by a single word
verbal subgroup of a group determined by a set of words

members.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.closure / Subgroup.normalClosure (used to build it); Mathlib has no verbal subgroups. `commutator` / `lowerCentralSeries` are only special cases.
members.code:
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = g}
members.docstring:
The verbal subgroup `W(G)` of a group `G` determined by a set `W` of laws: the subgroup
generated by all values `w(g₀, g₁, …)` of the words `w ∈ W` on `G`.
members.meaning: The subgroup generated by all values of the words in W under assignments of the variables in G.
members.name: verbalSubgroup
members.title: Conjecture 4.11

members.closest_existing_considered: commutator / Subgroup.commutator / lowerCentralSeries (special cases of verbal subgroups, but no general notion); Subgroup.normalClosure and Subgroup.closure (used as building block).
members.code:
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G, φ w = g}
members.docstring:
The *verbal subgroup* `W(G)` of a group `G` determined by a set of words `W`, i.e. of
elements of the free group on the countably many variables `x₀, x₁, …`: the subgroup of `G`
generated by all values `w(g₀, g₁, …)` of the words `w ∈ W` at elements `gᵢ ∈ G`, that is,
by all images `φ w` under homomorphisms `φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G`.
members.meaning: The subgroup generated by all images of words in W under homomorphisms FreeGroup ℕ →* G.
members.name: verbalSubgroup
members.title: Conjecture 3.5
members.why: Same closure, but the generating set is described via homomorphisms `φ : FreeGroup ℕ →* G` instead of assignments `f : ℕ → G` with `FreeGroup.lift f`; these give the same set of values because every such φ equals `FreeGroup.lift (φ ∘ of)` (FreeGroup.lift.unique), so the subgroups are propositionally (not definitionally) equal.

members.closest_existing_considered: Subgroup.normalClosure, Subgroup.closure (no verbal-subgroup notion in Mathlib).
members.code:
def verbalSubgroup (W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.normalClosure {g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = g}
members.docstring:
The *verbal subgroup* $W(G)$ of `G` determined by the set of words `W`: the subgroup of `G`
generated by all values $w(g_0, g_1, \dots)$ of words $w \in W$ in `G`. This subgroup is
normal (its generating set is closed under conjugation), so we use `Subgroup.normalClosure`
to record that.
members.meaning: The normal closure (equal to the closure) of the set of all values of words in W in G.
members.name: verbalSubgroup
members.title: Conjecture 4.72
members.why: Identical generating set `{g | ∃ w ∈ W, ∃ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f w = g}` but wrapped in `Subgroup.normalClosure` instead of `Subgroup.closure`; since the set of word-values is closed under conjugation (c * lift f w * c⁻¹ = lift (fun i => c * f i * c⁻¹) w), the normal closure equals the ordinary closure, so the subgroups are propositionally (not definitionally) equal.

members.closest_existing_considered: `commutator G` / `Subgroup.commutator` (only the special case v = [x₁,x₂]); `FreeGroup.lift` and `MonoidHom.range` (range of a single lift is not the verbal subgroup, one needs the union over all assignments). Test lemma `verbalSubgroup_commutator` confirms agreement with `commutator G`.
members.code:
def verbalSubgroup (v : FreeGroup ι) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Subgroup G :=
  Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun g : ι → G => FreeGroup.lift g v)
members.docstring:
The verbal subgroup $vG$ of $G$ determined by the word $v$: the subgroup generated by all
values $v(g_1, \dots, g_n)$ of $v$ in $G$. Here `FreeGroup.lift g v` is the value of the word
`v` at the assignment `g` of group elements to its variables.
members.meaning: The subgroup generated by all values FreeGroup.lift g v of the word v under assignments g of the variables in G.
members.name: verbalSubgroup
members.title: Conjecture 2.45
members.why: Takes a single word `v : FreeGroup ι` over an arbitrary index type ι (subgroup generated by the values of that one word), whereas the representative takes a set `W : Set (FreeGroup ℕ)` of words in countably many fixed variables; the parameter types differ so neither can replace the other (they agree only in the special case ι = ℕ, W = {v}).

groups.notes: The representative was changed from kourovka-2.45 to kourovka-4.11 because 2.45 is the odd one out: it takes a single word over an arbitrary index type ι, whereas the other three take a Set of words over the fixed countable variable set ℕ. 3.5, 4.11 and 4.72 all define the same subgroup W(G) (propositionally, not definitionally equal). No verbal-subgroup notion exists in Mathlib.

groups.concept: bi-invariant binary relation on a group
labels: bi-invariant binary relation on a group

members.closest_existing_considered: `MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G` (Mathlib, typeclass-based); `IsOrderedMonoid` (rejected: requires `CommMonoid`).
members.code:
def IsBiInvariant (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b x y : G, r a b → r (x * a * y) (x * b * y)
members.docstring:
A binary relation $r$ on a group $G$ is *bi-invariant* if $r(a, b)$ implies
$r(x a y, x b y)$ for all $x, y \in G$. A partial (resp. linear) ordering *of the
group* $G$ is a bi-invariant partial (resp. linear) order on $G$.
members.meaning: A relation r on a group such that r a b implies r (x*a*y) (x*b*y) for all x, y (invariance under left and right multiplication).
members.name: IsBiInvariant
members.title: Conjecture 1.35

members.closest_existing_considered: MulLeftMono G ∧ MulRightMono G (instance-based; used in an API test to show the two agree for a LinearOrder instance), IsOrderedMonoid (rejected: requires CommMonoid).
members.code:
def IsBiInvariant (r : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃a b : G⦄ (x y : G), r a b → r (x * a * y) (x * b * y)
members.docstring:
A binary relation $r$ on a group is *bi-invariant* (two-sided invariant) if
$r(a, b)$ implies $r(xay, xby)$ for all $x, y$.
members.meaning: r a b implies r (x*a*y) (x*b*y) for all x, y.
members.name: IsBiInvariant
members.title: Conjecture 2.28
members.why: Same body ∀ a b x y, r a b → r (x*a*y) (x*b*y); the only difference is that a b are strict-implicit binders, which does not change the underlying Prop.

members.closest_existing_considered: MulLeftMono/MulRightMono, IsOrderedMonoid (CommMonoid only), GroupCone (CommGroup only).
members.code:
def IsBiInvariant {G : Type*} [Group G] (le : G → G → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ a b x : G, le a b → le (x * a) (x * b)) ∧ (∀ a b x : G, le a b → le (a * x) (b * x))
members.docstring:
A binary relation `le` on a group is *two-sided invariant* if `le a b` implies
`le (x * a) (x * b)` and `le (a * x) (b * x)` for all `x`.
members.meaning: The relation is invariant under left multiplication and under right multiplication.
members.name: IsBiInvariant
members.title: Conjecture 3.20
members.why: States left-invariance ∧ right-invariance separately instead of the combined x*a*y form; equivalent since composing left and right invariance gives the two-sided form, and specializing y = 1 (resp. x = 1) with mul_one/one_mul recovers each half.

groups.notes: All three are the same notion (Covariant G G (·*·) r ∧ Covariant G G (swap (·*·)) r on an arbitrary relation). Mathlib has no relation-level version; MulLeftMono/MulRightMono are tied to an LE instance.

groups.concept: crossing number of a knot type
labels: crossing number of a knot
crossing number of a knot type

members.closest_existing_considered: None (the repo has graph crossing numbers only in unrelated contexts, if at all).
members.code:
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ' : ℝ → ℝ³) (_ : IsKnot γ') (_ : Isotopic γ γ') (u : ℝ³)
    (_ : IsRegularProjection γ' u), (crossings γ' u).encard
members.docstring:
The *crossing number* of the knot type of `γ`: the least number of crossings in a regular
projection of a knot ambient isotopic to `γ`.
members.meaning: Infimum of number of crossings over regular projections of knots ambient isotopic to γ.
members.name: crossingNumber
members.title: Is the minimum ropelength of a knot linear in its crossing number?

members.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib (Mathlib's Quandle file only mentions knots in prose)
members.code:
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set ℝ³) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (_ : IsSmoothKnotParam γ) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K (Set.range γ))
    (_ : IsRegularProjection γ), (crossings γ).encard
members.docstring:
The *crossing number* of the knot type of `K`: the minimal number of crossings in a knot
diagram of `K`, i.e. in a regular projection to the `xy`-plane of a smooth knot ambient isotopic
to `K`. Every direction of projection is covered, since rotations are ambient isotopies. The
value is `⊤` if `K` has no smooth representative (e.g. for a wild knot).
members.meaning: Infimum of number of crossings over regular xy-projections of smooth knots ambient isotopic to K.
members.name: crossingNumber
members.title: Ropelength problems
members.why: Takes a subset `K : Set ℝ³` rather than a parametrisation `γ : ℝ → ℝ³`, so it cannot replace the representative in its statement; moreover the infimum ranges over C^∞ representatives (`ContDiff ℝ ∞`) instead of C¹ ones, only the fixed xy-plane projection is used instead of all directions `u`, and crossings are counted as plane points with ≥2 preimages rather than parameter pairs. The mathematical value agrees for tame knots only via a nontrivial approximation/rotation argument, not by definition.

members.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (searched `rg -i knot|crossing`).
members.code:
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ : Circle → ℝ³) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ γ' : Circle → ℝ³,
    IsEmbedding γ' ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ) (Set.range γ') ∧
    IsRegularDiagram γ' ∧ (crossingSet γ').ncard = n}
members.docstring:
The **crossing number** of the knot type of the knot `γ`: the least number of crossings in a
regular diagram of a knot `γ'` whose image is ambient isotopic to that of `γ`. (Any regular
projection direction can be rotated to the vertical one by an ambient isotopy, so it suffices to
consider vertical projections.) For a knot type with no `C¹` representative (a wild knot) the set
below is empty and the value is `0`; such knot types have infinite ropelength.
members.meaning: The least number of crossings of a regular diagram of an embedded curve ambient isotopic to the given knot.
members.name: crossingNumber
members.title: Ropelength and crossing number: the constant in $L(K) \geq a \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$
members.why: Domain is `Circle → ℝ³` (not `ℝ → ℝ³`) and the value lives in `ℕ` via `sInf` (so wild knots get `0`) rather than in `ℕ∞` (where they get `⊤`); the minimisation is over topological embeddings with a C¹ regular vertical diagram and counts plane points with exactly two preimages via `ncard`, versus the representative's C¹ knots with arbitrary projection directions and parameter-pair crossings counted by `encard`.

groups.notes: All three are bespoke; none is in Mathlib. They differ in argument type (ℝ → ℝ³ vs Set ℝ³ vs Circle → ℝ³), value type (ℕ∞ vs ℕ), regularity class of representatives (C¹ vs C^∞), and whether all projection directions or just the vertical one are minimised over, so no pair is substitutable.

groups.concept: crossing-free straight-line drawing of a graph in the plane
labels: crossing-free straight-line drawing of a graph in the plane

members.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.UnitDistanceEmbeddable` (no crossing condition, fixed unit lengths); `IsPlanarDrawing` specialised to `segmentArcs f`.
members.code:
def IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  IsPlanarDrawing G f (segmentArcs f)
members.docstring:
`IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing G f` says that placing the vertices of `G` at the points `f v`
and drawing every edge as a straight segment gives a planar drawing of `G`
(a *Fáry embedding* of `G`).
members.meaning: The placement f with segment arcs forms a crossing-free drawing of G (a Fáry embedding).
members.name: IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing
members.title: Harborth's conjecture

members.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph and the repo for 'planar', 'drawing', 'crossing': only UnitDistance embeddings exist, which do not express crossing-freeness.
members.code:
def IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing : Prop :=
  Function.Injective p ∧
  (∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → p w ∈ segment ℝ (p u) (p v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
  (∀ u v x y, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y → s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) →
    segment ℝ (p u) (p v) ∩ segment ℝ (p x) (p y) ⊆ p '' ({u, v} ∩ {x, y}))
members.docstring:
`p` is a planar straight-line drawing of `G`: distinct vertices are drawn at distinct points,
no vertex lies on the segment drawing an edge unless it is an endpoint of that edge, and the
segments drawing two distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints.
members.meaning: Injective placement, no vertex on an edge segment unless an endpoint, and segments of distinct edges meeting only at common endpoints.
members.name: IsPlanarStraightLineDrawing
members.title: Strong Papadimitriou–Ratajczak conjecture
variables: variable {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (p : V → ℝ²)
members.why: Same injectivity, vertex-avoidance (stated contrapositively: `w ≠ u → w ≠ v → f w ∉ seg` vs `f w ∈ seg → w = u ∨ w = v`) and pairwise-intersection conditions; the representative's extra `exists_path` field is redundant since for adjacent (hence distinct, by injectivity, distinct-image) vertices the straight-line parametrisation is an injective path whose range is the segment.

members.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `segment ℝ`, `Path.segment`, `Function.Injective` (used as building blocks); FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Geometry/2d.lean has only convex-position predicates.
members.code:
def IsStraightLineDrawing (G : SimpleGraph V) (f : V → ℝ²) : Prop :=
  Function.Injective f ∧
    (∀ u v w, G.Adj u v → f w ∈ segment ℝ (f u) (f v) → w = u ∨ w = v) ∧
    ∀ u v x y, G.Adj u v → G.Adj x y → s(u, v) ≠ s(x, y) →
      segment ℝ (f u) (f v) ∩ segment ℝ (f x) (f y) ⊆ f '' ({u, v} ∩ {x, y})
members.docstring:
`f` is a crossing-free straight-line drawing of the simple graph `G` in the plane: the vertices are
placed at distinct points, every edge `{u, v}` is drawn as the closed line segment from `f u` to
`f v`, no such segment contains a vertex other than its two endpoints, and the segments of two
distinct edges meet only in the images of their common endpoints.
members.meaning: Injective placement, no vertex on a segment unless an endpoint, and segments of distinct edges meeting only at common endpoints.
members.name: IsStraightLineDrawing
members.title: Universal point set
members.why: Literally the same formula as the Papadimitriou–Ratajczak variant (only binder names differ); relative to the representative it drops the redundant `exists_path` field and states vertex-avoidance contrapositively, so it is logically equivalent but not syntactically defeq.

groups.notes: All three variants define the same predicate: injective vertex placement, no vertex in the interior of a foreign edge segment, and segments of distinct edges meeting only in images of common endpoints. The representative additionally carries an `exists_path` field (each edge segment is the range of an injective path), but this is automatically satisfied once `f` is injective (adjacent vertices are distinct, so `t ↦ lineMap (f u) (f v) t` is an injective path with range the segment), so it adds nothing. Variants 2 and 3 are literally identical to each other.

groups.concept: euler characteristic of a topological space (rational singular homology)
labels: euler characteristic of a topological space (via rational homology)
euler characteristic of a topological space (rational singular homology)

members.closest_existing_considered: Only a combinatorial Euler characteristic-like notion in IncidenceAlgebra (unrelated); nothing topological.
members.code:
noncomputable def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ k : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ k * bettiNumber X k
members.docstring:
The Euler characteristic $\chi(X) = \sum_k (-1)^k \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_k(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a
topological space `X`, as a finite sum over all `k`. For a compact manifold the Betti numbers are
finite and vanish above the dimension, so this is the usual Euler characteristic. (For a space
with infinitely many non-zero Betti numbers `finsum` returns `0`, but no such space occurs here.)
members.meaning: Finite sum over k of (−1)^k times the k-th rational Betti number.
members.name: eulerCharacteristic
members.title: Chern's conjecture (affine geometry)

members.closest_existing_considered: AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor (used); no `eulerCharacteristic`, `bettiNumber` or CW/simplicial-complex Euler characteristic exists.
members.code:
noncomputable def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ k : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ k * Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology X k)
members.docstring:
The Euler characteristic $\chi(X) = \sum_k (-1)^k \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_k(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a
topological space `X`.

The sum is a `finsum`, so it is the usual Euler characteristic whenever only finitely many rational
Betti numbers are non-zero, which is the case for compact manifolds.
members.meaning: Finite sum over k of (−1)^k finrank_ℚ H_k(X;ℚ).
members.name: eulerCharacteristic
members.title: Hopf conjecture
members.why: Same universe-polymorphic `X : Type u`, same coefficient object `ModuleCat.of ℚ (ULift.{u} ℚ)` in `ModuleCat.{u} ℚ`, same finsum `∑ᶠ k, (-1)^k * finrank`; the only difference is that the representative routes through the def `bettiNumber` whereas Hopf inlines `Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology X k)` with `rationalHomology` an abbrev for the identical homology object, so the two are definitionally equal.

members.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib for `eulerChar`/`EulerCharacteristic`; only unrelated notions exist (none for spaces or chain complexes).
members.code:
def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ n : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ n * Module.finrank ℚ (rationalHomology X n)
members.docstring:
The (rational) *Euler characteristic*
$\chi(X) = \sum_n (-1)^n \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_n(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a topological space `X`.
This is the intended value when the total rational homology of `X` is finite-dimensional
(for instance when `X` is rationally elliptic); otherwise it is a junk value.
members.meaning: Σ_n (−1)^n dim_ℚ H_n(X; ℚ) as a finite sum.
members.name: eulerCharacteristic
members.title: Halperin conjecture
members.why: Same alternating finsum of rational Betti numbers, but the coefficient object is `ModuleCat.of ℚ ℚ` instead of `ModuleCat.of ℚ (ULift.{0} ℚ)` (isomorphic, not equal, so finrank agreement needs transporting `ULift.moduleEquiv` through the homology functor), and the variant is restricted to `X : Type` (universe 0) whereas the representative is universe-polymorphic; on `Type` they agree, but the variant cannot replace the representative for spaces in higher universes.

groups.notes: All three are the standard rational Euler characteristic ∑ᶠ (-1)^k dim_ℚ H_k(X;ℚ) built on Mathlib's `singularHomologyFunctor` into `ModuleCat ℚ`, with `finsum` giving junk 0 when infinitely many Betti numbers are nonzero. Cherns and Hopf are definitionally the same (universe-polymorphic, `ULift.{u} ℚ` coefficients). Halperin agrees mathematically but is fixed to `X : Type` and uses `ℚ` rather than `ULift.{0} ℚ` as coefficients, so equality of Betti numbers goes through a functorial isomorphism rather than `rfl`; the Lean check for it is best-effort (untested lemma names `LinearEquiv.toModuleIso`, `Iso.toLinearEquiv`, `LinearEquiv.finrank_eq`).

groups.concept: graph minor (branch-set model)
labels: graph minor (branch-set model)

members.closest_existing_considered: `Matroid.IsMinor` (matroids, not graphs); `SimpleGraph.Subgraph`, `SimpleGraph.IsContained`/`⊑` (subgraph containment only, no contraction); `SimpleGraph.Connected` and `SimpleGraph.induce` are used as building blocks.
members.code:
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (B w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w w' ↦ Disjoint (B w) (B w')) ∧
    ∀ w w', H.Adj w w' → ∃ u ∈ B w, ∃ v ∈ B w', G.Adj u v
members.docstring:
The graph `H` is a *minor* of the graph `G` if `H` can be obtained from a subgraph of `G` by
contracting edges. Equivalently, and this is the form used here, there are *branch sets*
`B w ⊆ V(G)` for `w ∈ V(H)` which are pairwise disjoint and each induce a connected (hence
nonempty) subgraph of `G`, such that for every edge `w w'` of `H` some edge of `G` joins `B w`
to `B w'`.
members.meaning: There are pairwise disjoint vertex sets of G indexed by vertices of H, each inducing a connected subgraph, with an edge of G between the branch sets of every adjacent pair in H.
members.name: IsMinor
members.title: Apex graphs and Jørgensen's conjecture

members.closest_existing_considered: Matroid.IsMinor (matroids, not graphs); SimpleGraph.Subgraph / SimpleGraph.induce with Connected (used as building blocks); SimpleGraph.Subgraph.Connected. None expresses edge contraction/minor containment.
members.code:
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ f : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (f w)).Connected) ∧
    (Pairwise fun w₁ w₂ => Disjoint (f w₁) (f w₂)) ∧
    ∀ w₁ w₂, H.Adj w₁ w₂ → ∃ v₁ ∈ f w₁, ∃ v₂ ∈ f w₂, G.Adj v₁ v₂
members.docstring:
A graph `H` is a *minor* of a graph `G` if `G` contains a model of `H`: a family of pairwise
disjoint vertex sets `f w` of `G` (the *branch sets*), one for each vertex `w` of `H`, such that
every branch set induces a connected (in particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, and whenever
`w₁` and `w₂` are adjacent in `H` some vertex of `f w₁` is adjacent in `G` to some vertex of
`f w₂`.

Equivalently, `H` is isomorphic to a graph obtained from a subgraph of `G` by contracting edges
(each branch set is contracted to a single vertex).
members.meaning: There is a family of pairwise disjoint connected branch sets of G indexed by vertices of H with G-edges between branch sets of H-adjacent vertices.
members.name: IsMinor
members.title: Hadwiger conjecture (graph theory)
members.why: Term-for-term the same definition as the representative (branch sets f : W → Set V, connected induced subgraphs, Pairwise Disjoint, edge of G between branch sets of adjacent H-vertices); only bound-variable names differ.

members.closest_existing_considered: Matroid.IsMinor (matroids, not graphs); SimpleGraph.Subgraph / `≤` (subgraphs only, no contraction); SimpleGraph.Copy / IsContained (subgraph containment, no contraction).
members.code:
def IsMinor (H : SimpleGraph W) (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ A : W → Set V, (∀ w, (G.induce (A w)).Connected) ∧
    Pairwise (fun w w' => Disjoint (A w) (A w')) ∧
    ∀ ⦃w w'⦄, H.Adj w w' → ∃ u ∈ A w, ∃ v ∈ A w', G.Adj u v
members.docstring:
`IsMinor H G` means that the graph `H` is a *minor* of the graph `G`, i.e. `H` can be
obtained from `G` by deleting vertices, deleting edges and contracting edges.

We use the standard equivalent description by *branch sets*: there is a family `A` of pairwise
disjoint vertex sets `A w ⊆ V(G)`, indexed by the vertices `w` of `H`, each inducing a connected
(in particular nonempty) subgraph of `G`, such that whenever `w` and `w'` are adjacent in `H`
there is an edge of `G` between `A w` and `A w'`.
members.meaning: There are pairwise disjoint connected branch sets in G indexed by vertices of H with an edge of G between branch sets for every edge of H.
members.name: IsMinor
members.title: GNRS conjecture
members.why: Same existential over branch sets W → Set V with connected induced subgraphs, Pairwise Disjoint, and an edge of G between branch sets for each H-edge; the only difference is the strict-implicit binder `∀ ⦃w w'⦄` instead of `∀ w w'`, which is cosmetic and does not affect definitional equality.

groups.notes: All three files define the graph-minor relation via the identical branch-set model (W-indexed family of pairwise disjoint sets of vertices of G, each inducing a connected subgraph, with a G-edge between branch sets for every H-edge). Mathlib has no SimpleGraph minor notion (only Matroid.IsMinor), so this is a good candidate for a shared definition. Note this model relation is the standard 'H is isomorphic to a minor of G' relation (it does not require nonempty branch sets separately since Connected implies Nonempty).

labels: pro-orderable group (o*-group)

members.closest_existing_considered: No existing notion of orderable / bi-orderable / O*-group found (rg over Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for 'orderable', 'bi-invariant', 'LeftOrdered', 'BiOrdered').
members.docstring:
A group $G$ is *pro-orderable* if each of its partial orderings can be extended to
a linear ordering. That is, for every bi-invariant partial order $\le$ on $G$ there
is a bi-invariant linear order $\preceq$ on $G$ such that $a \le b$ implies
$a \preceq b$ for all $a, b \in G$.
members.meaning: Every bi-invariant partial order on the group extends to a bi-invariant linear order.
members.name: IsProOrderable
members.title: Conjecture 1.35

members.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib; quantifying over PartialOrder G / LinearOrder G instances with @MulLeftMono was considered and rejected as less readable.
members.docstring:
A group is *pro-orderable* (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 1.35) if every bi-invariant partial
order on it can be extended to a bi-invariant linear order.
members.meaning: Every bi-invariant partial order extends to a bi-invariant linear order.
members.name: IsProOrderable
members.title: Conjecture 2.28
members.why: Same statement; the only difference is that IsBiInvariant uses strict-implicit binders ⦃a b⦄ instead of explicit ones, which is ignored by definitional equality.

members.closest_existing_considered: none (searched Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib for orderable/bi-order notions)
members.docstring:
A group is *pro-orderable* (an $O^*$-group) if every two-sided invariant partial order
on it can be extended to a two-sided invariant linear order.
members.meaning: Every bi-invariant partial order on G extends to a bi-invariant linear order.
members.name: IsProOrderable
members.title: Conjecture 3.20
members.why: Quantifies over PartialOrder/LinearOrder structures instead of relations with IsPartialOrder/IsLinearOrder, and defines bi-invariance as left-invariance ∧ right-invariance instead of two-sided r a b → r (x*a*y) (x*b*y); both differences are logically equivalent (structures ↔ relations via the obvious constructions, and two-sided invariance ↔ left ∧ right invariance by specializing y=1/x=1 and composing).

groups.notes: All three variants formalize the Mal'cev–Fuchs O*-group notion: every bi-invariant partial order on G extends to a bi-invariant linear order on G. Variants 1 and 2 quantify over relations with IsPartialOrder/IsLinearOrder; variant 3 quantifies over PartialOrder/LinearOrder structures and splits bi-invariance into left and right invariance, which is logically equivalent (take y = 1 / x = 1, resp. compose left and right invariance).
